text: He says many people complain of joint pain, lower-back pain, and pain around the neck or upper spine.
He says many patients consult neurologists, neurosurgeons, or pain specialists, and he argues that an underlying bone problem is sometimes overlooked.
He claims that weak bones can hurt even without carrying heavy loads or doing weight-bearing activity.
He repeats that, in his view, pain may occur even without lifting or obvious mechanical strain.
He attributes this to the effect of gravity on weak bone and says this creates friction or compression.
He says this friction can make bones and joints press more closely together, and he links this to the loss of height that can occur with age.
He argues that poor bone strength may involve inadequate mineralization, low protein, insufficient calcium, or vitamin D deficiency.
He compares weakened bone to cartilage, saying it becomes easier to compress and may contribute to shortening or structural change.
He says pain can then become a persistent symptom in patients with these underlying problems.
He emphasizes that treatment should focus on strengthening bone and correcting deficiencies before only treating the pain itself.
He concludes: treat the cause, and the symptom will improve.
